items.prompt: After shallow=original.copy(), both dictionaries reference the same nested tags list. What does appending through shallow do?

options.text: It can only change a new fully independent nested list
options.why: A shallow copy does not recursively copy nested objects.

options.text: It always raises because copied dictionaries are immutable
options.why: Both ordinary dictionaries and lists remain mutable.

options.text: It changes the shared list visible through both records
options.why: Both outer dictionaries hold a reference to the same list.

options.text: It replaces every key in the original dictionary
options.why: Appending to one nested list does not replace outer keys.

items.explanation: An outer copy duplicates the mapping but preserves references to nested objects. Test mutation at the level where shared state exists.
